segs.text: That white line behind a plane is not smoke.
It is a cloud, and the plane makes it by itself.
Jet engines burn fuel, and the exhaust is full of hot water vapor.
Up at cruising height, the air is colder than minus thirty degrees.
The hot vapor meets that cold air and turns into tiny ice crystals.
Specks of soot give the vapor something to cling to.
In dry air, the ice vanishes in seconds.
In humid air, the line can stay for hours and spread wide.
A long trail means the air up there is full of moisture.
So that white line is not smoke. It is a cloud.
